question.text: Under Section 18A of SCRA, when are contracts in derivatives considered legal and valid?

answer.text: When traded on a recognized stock exchange and settled on the clearing house of such exchange as per its rules and bye-laws
When entered into between any two parties with a written agreement
When approved by SEBI on a case-by-case basis
When the contract value exceeds a minimum threshold set by the government

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 18A states that contracts in derivatives shall be legal and valid if they are (a) traded on a recognized stock exchange, and (b) settled on the clearing house of the recognized stock exchange, in accordance with the rules and bye-laws of such exchange. The Trap: Both conditions are required together; satisfying only one of them is not sufficient under Section 18A. Note: The statutory test under Section 18A is the dual requirement of recognized-exchange trading and clearing-house settlement per the exchange's rules and bye-laws.
